newsitem.title: UK: UK consumer group sees fewer Brit Gas complaints.
newsitem.headline: UK consumer group sees fewer Brit Gas complaints.

text.p: Britain's Gas Consumer Council (GCC) on Monday said it was now receiving fewer consumer complaints about Centrica's British Gas operations.
In a statement accompanying its 1996 annual report, the council said the number of complaints about British Gas Trading fell seven percent in March.

There was still a 22 percent rise to a record 7,777 over the three-month period from January to March, when complaints about British Gas Services and British Gas Energy Centres had already begun to fall.
Most of complaints on British Gas Trading were over faulty bills.

The company said this was the result of teething problems with a new computer system which had to be implemented more quickly than scheduled due to the rapid introduction of competition in the UK domestic gas market.
The opening-up started in April 1996 in the south west of England and has been expanded earlier this year to other parts in the south.
Nationwide competition is envisaged next year.
The Gas Consumer Council's chairwoman, Jenny Kirkpatrick, stressed that all consumers, including poor families using pre-payment metres, should benefit from competition.
The consumer council found earlier this year that low-income consumers in the competitive market are charged as much as 34 percent more for their gas.

Speaking just over a week after Labour's election victory, Kirkpatrick said: "We want the new government to ensure that regulation balances the introduction of domestic competition with consumer protection."
